chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Ribat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Prophet (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) said to Sa'd ibn Ubada: 'Indeed, God has established a limit (hadd) for every thing, and He has established a penalty (hadd) for everyone who transgresses a limit from the limits of God, Mighty and Majestic, and He has made what falls short of four witnesses a veil [of concealment] for the Muslims.'

key_terms.الأَرْبَعَة الشُّهَدَاء: The four witnesses — the strict evidentiary standard required to prosecute certain offenses in Islamic law
key_terms.تَعَدَّى: Transgression — violating the boundaries set by God
key_terms.حَدّ / حُدُود: Hadd/Hudud — divinely prescribed limits and their corresponding fixed penalties (e.g., for theft, adultery, false accusation)
key_terms.مَسْتُور: Veiled/concealed — legally obscured, not subject to prosecution

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about hudud (divine limits) and the requirement of four witnesses in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a saying of the Prophet (SAWW) to Sa'd ibn Ubada, one of the leading Ansar companions, establishing three foundational principles of Islamic criminal law: (1) every offense has a prescribed penalty; (2) those who transgress divine limits face mandatory punishment; and (3) the evidentiary threshold of four witnesses for certain offenses (particularly illicit sexual conduct) functions as a mercy — without sufficient witnesses, the offense is 'veiled' and not prosecuted. This reflects the Islamic legal principle of maintaining social order while simultaneously protecting individuals from harsh punishments in the absence of overwhelming proof.
